overview: RIC-920 is a pit droid built by Industrial Automaton, documented across Phantom Menace · Clone Wars. A wheeled pit droid model used in racing circuits and industrial maintenance bays from the Boonta Eve Classic onward.
history:
RIC-920 belongs to the pit droid class manufactured by Industrial Automaton, one of the most recognizable automaton designs documented across galactic history. RIC-920 wheeled pit droids serve racing circuits with faster mobility than standard pit droids. Industrial Automaton factory schematics document the pit droid platform lineage that produced RIC-920, scaling from boutique Core workshops to wartime foundries on Geonosis, Skako Minor, and Nar Shaddaa. Factory logs, maintenance manuals, and holodrama archives all treat RIC-920 as more than a serial number—a unit whose choices and failures moved empires. Sources spanning all nine saga films, animated series, Knights of the Old Republic, Knights of the Old Republic II, The Old Republic, and the ancient Sith Empire reference this design lineage.

Early prototypes and predecessor chassis from the Old Republic era established the engineering tradition that produced RIC-920. Excavations on Taris, Dxun, and Dromund Kaas recovered pit droid chassis predating the Clone Wars by centuries; Sith Empire war factories and Rakatan reverse-engineering vaults copied Industrial Automaton subsystems, spreading design language across millennia before RIC-920 rolled off modern lines. significance:
Engineering analysis of RIC-920 highlights why pit droid designs succeed: modular parts, clear firmware roles, and production lines scaled to wartime demand. Technicians praise RIC-920's modular pit droid subsystems: field-replaceable limbs, redundant processors, and firmware packages that slicers and mechanics exploit in scrap yards centuries after initial rollout. Technicians praise Industrial Automaton documentation; slicers praise its predictable security flaws—both keep RIC-920 relevant in scrap yards centuries later. New Republic certification boards still debate which pit droid subroutines require sentience review under the Galactic Rights Charter.

Droid rights activists cite RIC-920 when arguing that personality matrices, memory wipes, and restraining bolts can be torture or enslavement. Droid-rights tribunals cite RIC-920 when debating memory wipes, restraining bolts, and sentience; parallels to L3-37's Kessel uprising and C-3PO's testimony echo through every pit droid rights petition involving Industrial Automaton personality matrices. C-3PO's testimony before Bail Organa and L3-37's Kessel uprising belong to the same moral conversation as RIC-920's service record. Whether RIC-920 is property or person remains unsettled law on a hundred worlds.

The galactic impact of RIC-920 exceeds production statistics: this unit type altered battles, treaties, and cultural memory. Historians argue galactic history pivots on units like RIC-920; sources spanning all nine saga films, Clone Wars, Rebels, Mandalorian, Andor, KOTOR, KOTOR II, SWTOR, and the ancient Sith Empire treat surviving memory cores as primary sources. Without units like RIC-920, key missions—from Death Star data recovery to Separatist invasions—would have unfolded differently or failed entirely. Museums on Coruscant, Mandalore, and Nar Shaddaa display Industrial Automaton chassis as icons of industrial civilization and its costs.
